subject: Trajectory MAP: evaluation triggers & reservation term proposal
messages:
From: Elena Petrova <elena@nimbusai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jack Reynolds <jack@tessera.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Trajectory MAP: evaluation triggers & reservation term proposal

Hi Aditya / Jack —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move from POC to a tightly-scoped evaluation that aligns to a mutual action plan (MAP) and then into a dedicated reservation if the eval metrics are met. I attached a rough MAP draft (MAP_NimbusAI_v2.xlsx) that outlines three milestones:

- M1 (2 weeks): integration + 1k daily inference calls, latency < 120ms p50
- M2 (6 weeks): steady-state traffic ramp to 50k monthly calls, cost target <$0.0025/token equivalent
- M3 (12 weeks): production readiness with autoscale + KV-cache validation

We are expecting to size a GPU pool to support the ramp above. Initial ask from our infra team is for an 8x A100-equivalent reservation during the first 90 days, with ability to burst for traffic spikes. Key commercial questions for us: pricing for a 90d reserved slice vs longer-term 12–24 month commit, how discounts ramp with committed GPU equivalents, and what burst clauses look like (how much free burst, duration, and overage pricing).

Can you put together suggested reservation terms that tie to the MAP milestones (pricing, commit ramp, discounts, burst behavior)? We want the MAP to be the gating instrument for each milestone and for cost/commit adjustments.

Happy to jump on a call next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena
Sr. Ops Lead | NimbusAI

Attachments: MAP_NimbusAI_v2.xlsx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Petrova <elena@nimbusai.com>, Jack Reynolds <jack@tessera.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trajectory MAP: evaluation triggers & reservation term proposal

Elena —

Appreciate the clear MAP — this is exactly the right way to structure the evaluation. I reviewed the draft and sketched a reservation proposal that ties commercial terms to the MAP milestones. I attached a one-page summary (Reservation_Term_Summary.pdf). High level:

- Baseline sizing: 8 A100-equivalents reserved to support M1–M2 ramp.
- Term options: 90-day evaluation reserve (short reserve) OR convert to 12- or 24-month committed capacity once M3 is achieved.
- Pricing/discounts: 90d reserve = list price with a 5% intro credit; 12-mo commit = list - 12% discount; 24-mo commit = list - 20% discount. Additional scale discount: +5% if commit >= 16 GPUs.
- Ramp mechanics: MAP milestone sign-offs trigger conversion credits. If M2 achieves target traffic by week 6 and you convert within 15 days, we apply a one-time conversion credit equivalent to 10% of the 90d reservation invoice.
- Burst clause: we propose two-tier burst handling: free burst up to 25% of committed capacity for up to 45 days total during the first 90 days; thereafter bursts billed at on-demand up to a 50% cap of committed capacity in any 24-hr window. Overage billing uses on-demand SKU pricing in Nimbus_SKU_pricing.csv.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If you’re comfortable with the structure, sign the MAP + reservation LOI so we can lock the short-reserve and schedule the dedicated pool.
2) We (Redwood) spin up the 8-GPU pool in your chosen region; your infra team verifies integration (M1).
3) If M2/M3 pass, we execute the conversion amendment to commit term (12/24mo) per the discount schedule above.

I’ve CC’d Lauren to help with billing cadence and to initiate the LOI/DocuSign flow if you want to proceed. Happy to discuss any of the suggested numbers.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Reservation_Term_Summary.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trajectory MAP: evaluation triggers & reservation term proposal (pricing confirmation)

Aditya / team —

Reviewed the numbers and here are the firm pricing inputs we should ship back to Nimbus:

1) Reserved SKU economics (monthly equivalent per A100-eq):
   - List: $9,500 / GPU / month (baseline reference for on-prem-like reserved pricing)
   - 90d short-reserve: bill pro-rata of list; apply a one-time 5% short-reserve credit as Aditya suggested.
2) Committed discounts (applied to monthly list):
   - 12-month, >=8 GPUs: 12% off list (effective $8,360/GPU/mo)
   - 24-month, >=8 GPUs: 20% off list (effective $7,600/GPU/mo)
   - Volume breakpoint: if commit >=16 GPUs, additional 5% off (stacked)
3) Conversion credit: when MAP milestone M2 is validated and customer signs conversion within 15 days, apply credit = 10% of the 90d invoices (credit applied to first invoice post-conversion).
4) Burst policy (recommended):
   - Intro free burst: up to 25% of committed capacity for up to 45 days total in the first 90d window (helps dev/test spikes during early ramp).
   - Post-intro bursts: billed at on-demand (list/24hr-pricing) with one-week smoothing to avoid flash spikes.
   - Hard cap: charge for bursts beyond 50% of committed capacity in any 24-hr window at a premium (1.4x on-demand rate) — we should only use premium for persistent overages.
5) SLA/ops notes:
   - We will reserve buffer capacity on our infra side for the initial pool spin-up; on final conversion to committed term we will schedule a change freeze window for relocation/optimization (48–72 hours).

If that looks good I’ll prepare a pricing worksheet (Nimbus_SKU_pricing.csv) and we can include the table in the LOI. Happy to tighten numbers if the customer is sensitive to per-GPU/months — we have some flexibility on the 12% tier if they need it for procurement.

—Marcus
Director, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Trajectory MAP: evaluation triggers & reservation term proposal

Elena / Jack —

Thanks for the quick review. Per Marcus / Lauren / Neha’s input we’ve finalized the proposal and attached the pricing worksheet (Nimbus_SKU_pricing.csv) and reservation summary (Reservation_Term_Summary.pdf). TL;DR of the commercial MAP-driven workflow we propose:

- Start: Execute the short-reserve LOI to lock an 8x A100-equivalent pool for the 90d eval window. LOI captures the MAP milestones and conversion mechanics.
- Milestone triggers: M1/M2/M3 verification (as in your MAP) will be done via shared runbook and joint sign-off (we’ll use the HubSpot deal and shared Drive doc for evidence).
- Conversion: If M2 meets targets and Nimbus elects to convert to a committed term within 15 days, we apply a credit equal to 10% of the 90d billing and convert to either 12- or 24-mo pricing (12% / 20% discount).
- Burst: Intro free burst up to 25% for 45 days in the first 90d; thereafter bursts billed at on-demand with the caps Marcus outlined.

Action items:
1) I’ve created the LOI in DocuSign (link below). If you’re ready, sign and we’ll schedule the dedicated pool spin-up.
   - DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/ND-4521-reservation
2) Please confirm region (us-west-2 or us-east-1) so infra can pre-wire capacity.
3) Share any procurement constraints (PO cadence, required invoice terms) and Lauren will align billing cadence.

If helpful, I can set a 30-minute alignment call Friday to walk through the MAP timeline and conversion examples.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
